c.tagline: France's gastronomic capital, built on two rivers and Renaissance light.

taxi.fareNote: Official taxis are metered and wait at ranks outside major stations; street-hailing is uncommon, so ride-hail apps (Uber, Bolt, FreeNow) are widely used and often cheaper.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number reaching police, fire, and ambulance; 15 is the SAMU medical line and 17 the police.

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing around Part-Dieu and Bellecour; caution in parts of La Guillotière at night

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed Renaissance old town below Fourvière hill, a warren of cobbled streets, traboule passageways, bouchon restaurants, and the Saint-Jean cathedral; best for first-timers who want history within walking distance.

The central peninsula between the Rhône and Saône rivers, home to Place Bellecour, the opera, department stores, and the densest cluster of restaurants and cafes; the convenient walkable base for a first visit.
The steep former silk-weavers' hill, now a bohemian village of artist studios, indie boutiques, leafy squares, and a lively daily market; suits travelers after arts, character, and a local feel.
A regenerated former docklands at the tip of the peninsula where the rivers meet, with the striking Musée des Confluences, a waterfront mall, and modern architecture; calmer and good for families.
A buzzing, multicultural quarter across the Rhône packed with cheap eats, student bars, and late-night spots; suits younger travelers who want nightlife and diversity on a budget.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout the city.

transit.hours: The Métro runs roughly 5:00am to 12:30am (until ~1:00am on Fri–Sat); Pleine Lune night buses cover the late hours on weekends.
transit.note: Two funiculars (ficelles) climb from Vieux Lyon up to Fourvière and Saint-Just and are part of the standard TCL network.
transit.pay: The network is run by TCL. Buy a single ticket (€2.00, ~US$2.20), a 10-ride carnet, or a day pass at metro machines and tabacs, or use the TCL app; contactless bank cards also work on validators. One ticket covers metro, tram, funicular, and bus with free transfers within an hour.

transit.m: Rhônexpress tram to Part-Dieu (~30 min, every 15 min)
Taxi to city center (30-40 min, flat fare)

tip.r: Service is included by law (service compris); rounding up or leaving a few euros for good service is appreciated but not expected.
